sections.h2: Where is Enfield and how is the town laid out?
sections.html:
Enfield is a Hartford County town on the Massachusetts line, with the Connecticut River along its western edge. It belongs to the Capitol Planning Region and covers 34.2 square miles, of which 0.93 is water.

Longmeadow and East Longmeadow, Massachusetts, border it to the north, Somers lies to the east, and East Windsor and Ellington lie to the south. Suffield and Windsor Locks are across the river to the west. The 2020 Census counted 42,141 residents, and elevation is about 138 feet.

Because Enfield is large in area, houses range from compact village lots to rural parcels, and the buyer pool changes from one section to the next.

sections.h2: What is the history of Enfield?
sections.html:
Enfield was first settled in 1679 by the brothers Robert and John Pease from Salem, and it began as part of Massachusetts. The Podunk people had lived here before and had two villages, Scitico and Nameroke.

The town was incorporated in Massachusetts in 1683. In 1749, after a lawsuit showed that a surveyor's error had placed it inside the wrong colony, Enfield became part of Connecticut. The preacher Jonathan Edwards delivered his sermon "Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God" here during the Great Awakening.

The modern town was formed by merging Enfield, Thompsonville and Hazardville. In the nineteenth century the town was known for two industries. Colonel Augustus Hazard ran a gunpowder company in Powder Hollow from the 1830s to the 1910s, and Orrin Thompson built carpet mills in Thompsonville and housing for the workers, much of which still stands.

sections.h2: What are the sections and neighborhoods of Enfield?
sections.html:
Enfield has five traditional sections: Enfield Village, Thompsonville, Hazardville, Scitico and Sherwood Village. Within and around them are named neighborhoods that sellers use when describing a house.

  • Thompsonville: the urban town center on the river, with Victorian houses along Pearl Street and boat launches onto the Connecticut River.
  • Hazardville: named for Colonel Hazard, with a village center on Hazard Avenue, Powder Hollow Park and the Enfield Public Library.
  • Enfield Historic District: along Enfield Street (U.S. Route 5), with homes from the mid-eighteenth century on and a Greek Revival church.
  • Scitico and Green Manor: the eastern suburb with winding roads, cul-de-sacs and sidewalks, about 4.5 miles from I-91.
  • Shaker Pines: lakeside houses on a lake the Shakers built to power a mill.
  • Presidential Section: streets named for U.S. presidents, with mid-sized to large houses.

Others include Crescent Lake, North Thompsonville, The Laurels and Southwood Acres.

sections.h2: What does a historic house in Enfield mean for a sale?
sections.html:
Part of Enfield's housing is genuinely old, so sellers of historic or early houses should expect buyers to look closely at age. The Enfield Town Meetinghouse, built in 1773, is on the National Register of Historic Places, as is the Enfield Historic District along Route 5.

The Bigelow-Sanford Carpet Company buildings in Thompsonville are also listed and now serve as apartments called Bigelow Commons. If your house is in or near the historic district, ask the town's land use staff whether any rules apply to exterior work before you plan repairs. Whatever its age, a buyer's inspector will look at the roof, wiring, heating system and foundation, and findings there can slow a conventional sale.

sections.h2: What parks, schools and transit serve Enfield?
sections.html:
Enfield Public Schools operates the town's public schools, with Enfield High School as the sole high school and John F. Kennedy Middle School as the middle school. Asnuntuck Community College, opened here in 1972, is a two-year college, and the Capitol Region Education Council runs a magnet school in town.

The public park list includes:

  • Scantic River State Park, for canoeing, kayaking and fishing
  • Powder Hollow Park, with baseball fields and trails
  • Hazardville Park and Green Manor Recreational Area
  • Mark Twain Recreational Area and Brainerd Park

Connecticut Transit buses connect Enfield and Thompsonville to Hartford, and a bus link to the Pioneer Valley Transit Authority serves Springfield, Massachusetts. The town also runs an in-town bus called Magic Carpet, started in 2013. Ask the town about current service, since schedules change.

sections.h2: What is in Enfield's tax and assessment picture?
sections.html:
Call the Enfield Tax Collector and the Assessor, or visit the town website at enfield-ct.gov, for the current bill dates, the mill rate and the exact payoff for your parcel.

Two points apply to Connecticut towns in general. The Grand List is a yearly record of taxable property, and towns revalue every five years, as the East Haven assessor's page explains. A new assessment changes the tax a buyer will carry, so ask Enfield's assessor when the next one takes effect.

Current tax bill and due datesTax Collector
Assessed value and exemptionsAssessor
Zoning, permits and code issuesTown land use and building staff

Unpaid taxes on your property are settled from your sale proceeds at closing, so request a written payoff early.

sections.h2: What does the state require when you sell in Enfield?
sections.html:
Connecticut requires the grantor, or the grantor's attorney or agent, to file a real estate conveyance tax return when the deed is recorded, and tax is due when the price is $2,000 or more unless an exemption applies. Enfield is town code 049 on the Department of Revenue Services list.

Some towns file electronically through the state's myCTREC system, and others file on paper with the town clerk. The Enfield Town Clerk can tell you which applies. State exemptions that matter to sellers include:

  • A conveyance between spouses.
  • A deed in lieu of foreclosure on a principal residence.
  • A principal residence sold for less than the mortgages and priority tax or sewer liens against it.
  • A principal residence with a deteriorated concrete foundation from pyrrhotite, after a professional engineer's written evaluation.

An exemption needs its code on the return and may need an attachment. Your closing attorney can confirm which apply.

sections.h2: What should an Enfield seller gather before asking for offers?
sections.html:
A prepared seller closes faster, and a short list covers most of what a title company will ask for.

  • The deed or the estate papers showing who may sign.
  • A written tax payoff from the Enfield Tax Collector.
  • Payoff statements for any mortgage or lien.
  • Any lease, if tenants live in the house.
  • Names of the electric, water and heating suppliers for final readings.

If you are missing a piece, tell us anyway. We can often work around gaps in the paperwork.

sections.h2: What do Enfield sellers usually face, and how does a cash sale work?
sections.html:
Enfield sellers may be handling an older house that needs work, an inherited property, a rental, or a loan that has fallen behind. A cash sale removes the repairs and showings from the process.

  • You tell us the address and the condition of the house.
  • We review it and make an offer for the house as it stands.
  • If you accept, a title company or attorney prepares the deed and the state return.
  • Taxes, liens and payoffs come out of the proceeds.

We do not name a price before reviewing the property, and you can compare any offer with a listing.

faqs.a: Enfield is in Hartford County, Connecticut, on the border with Massachusetts.

faqs.q: How did Enfield become part of Connecticut?
faqs.a: In 1749, after a lawsuit found that a surveyor's error had put the town in the wrong colony, Enfield seceded from Massachusetts and joined Connecticut.

faqs.q: What are the main sections of Enfield?
faqs.a: The five sections are Enfield Village, Thompsonville, Hazardville, Scitico and Sherwood Village.

faqs.q: When are Enfield property taxes due?
faqs.a: The tax office can also give you a payoff figure for closing.

faqs.q: Do I owe the Connecticut conveyance tax when I sell in Enfield?
faqs.a: Usually yes, if the price is $2,000 or more and no exemption applies. The return is filed when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I sell an old Enfield house as it is?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can purchase an older house in its current condition, with no repairs required from you.
